paragraphs: A neural network can fit its training examples extremely closely and still predict new examples accurately. This phenomenon, called benign overfitting, challenges the idea that fitting training data too well necessarily harms generalization. The paper studies it in XOR-type classification problems with randomly flipped labels, moving beyond earlier analyses centered on problems whose best possible classifier is linear.

The authors analyze an overparameterized, two-layer ReLU convolutional neural network trained with gradient descent. They establish a condition involving the number of training examples and the signal-to-noise ratio under which the network approaches Bayes-optimal accuracy: the best accuracy permitted by the underlying data distribution. The result therefore connects successful learning to both the amount and quality of available information.

A matching lower bound establishes the other side of this condition. When it fails, the trained network remains a fixed positive amount below Bayes-optimal accuracy. Together, the results characterize a boundary between successful and unsuccessful learning in the studied setting, including XOR problems with strongly correlated features.
icml-2024-benign-overfitting-in-two-laye.tldr: The paper identifies when an overparameterized ReLU CNN can learn noisy XOR data nearly optimally, and proves a matching failure boundary.

paragraphs: Training algorithms favor some solutions over others even without an explicit instruction to do so. This implicit bias can help networks generalize, but good predictions on ordinary examples do not automatically imply resistance to adversarial perturbations. The paper investigates whether the same training tendency can support both properties when the network architecture changes.

The starting point is an earlier result for clustered data with weak correlations between clusters. In that setting, a shallow ReLU network trained by gradient flow generalizes well but remains vulnerable to small adversarial attacks, even though a more robust shallow classifier exists. This separates what the architecture can represent from what its training procedure actually selects.

The authors extend analyses of neuron alignment to shallow networks using polynomial ReLU activations. They show that these networks, when trained by gradient flow in the analyzed setting, can both generalize and resist adversarial attacks. The finding makes the interaction between data structure and activation design central: implicit bias can support robustness, but its effects depend on the architecture and problem being studied.
icml-2024-can-implicit-bias-imply-advers.tldr: For the analyzed setting, polynomial ReLU activations allow gradient-flow training of shallow networks to support both generalization and adversarial robustness.

paragraphs: Many naturally occurring protein sequences remain uncharacterized, creating a large pool of possible enzymes for useful chemical reactions. Experimentally screening that pool requires substantial time, money, and labor. CLIPZyme addresses the computational screening problem: using information about a desired reaction to identify promising enzyme candidates.

The method learns representations of enzyme structures and reaction pairs through a contrastive training objective. This aligns the two kinds of representation so that a reaction can be matched with relevant enzymes. The approach matters because it connects the chemical transformation being sought directly to structural information about proteins, providing a way to search a large candidate collection computationally.

Because there is no standard computational baseline for this task, the authors compare CLIPZyme with existing enzyme commission predictors adapted for screening. They report improved performance when reaction information is limited, with a BEDROC85 score of 44.69%. They also evaluate combining the methods and demonstrate generalization to unseen reactions and protein clusters. These findings concern computational screening performance and the ability to extend beyond familiar examples.
icml-2024-clipzyme-reaction-conditioned-.tldr: CLIPZyme aligns enzyme structures with reactions to improve computational enzyme screening, including cases with limited reaction information.

paragraphs: Determining whether a language model trained on a particular document is difficult when only its outputs are accessible. Existing methods rely on the model naturally memorizing some of that document. This paper investigates copyright traps: deliberately inserted fictitious passages intended to make training-data use detectable even when ordinary content leaves little detectable trace.

The authors conduct a randomized controlled experiment by placing traps in books and training a 1.3-billion-parameter model from scratch. They first establish that existing methods cannot detect the target model's use of the original content. They then test whether inserted material changes that outcome. Medium-length trap sentences remain undetectable with existing methods even when repeated 100 times.

Longer passages repeated many times are more effective, reaching a reported detection AUC of 0.75. This shows that successful traps depend on their construction; repetition alone did not make the tested shorter passages detectable. The controlled design also supports causal analysis of memorization and sequence properties, including repetition and perplexity, extending the contribution beyond detecting the use of copyrighted content.
icml-2024-copyright-traps-for-large-lang.tldr: Controlled experiments show that long, heavily repeated fictitious passages can reveal training-data use where ordinary content and shorter repeated traps remain undetectable.

paragraphs: Training large neural networks is expensive, and growing a smaller network during training offers a possible way to reduce that expense. The difficulty is understanding how growth changes the learning process. Deep Fusion combines a theoretical account of those changes with a practical approach that initializes larger networks using pretrained smaller networks.

The theoretical framework uses backward error analysis to examine the dynamics of growth partway through training. Its purpose is to guide how the transition should be handled, rather than treating network expansion as an isolated architectural operation. Deep Fusion also allows pretrained initializations from diverse sources, broadening the smaller networks that can contribute to a larger model.

Experiments support the framework's usefulness for choosing how to apply Deep Fusion. With carefully optimized training dynamics, the method reduces training time and resource consumption without sacrificing performance. Across the reported NLP tasks and T5 model sizes, the authors also observe improved generalization. The results tie the efficiency gains to how growth is managed during learning, alongside the reuse of pretrained parameters.
icml-2024-deep-fusion-efficient-network-.tldr: Deep Fusion uses pretrained smaller networks and a theory of mid-training growth to reduce training costs while preserving or improving reported performance.

paragraphs: DFlow targets high-fidelity audio waveform generation, where both sound quality and synthesis speed matter. The proposed framework brings together a normalizing flow and a denoising autoencoder in a single model. Its central contribution is a structure designed to integrate their capabilities and improve on standard normalizing-flow models.

The experiments assess both perceived quality and computational speed. DFlow achieves the highest reported mean opinion score among the existing methods considered on commonly used datasets. It also has the fastest synthesis speed among the likelihood-based models in the comparison. These are distinct findings: the quality comparison covers the evaluated methods, while the speed claim applies specifically to likelihood models.

The authors additionally test whether the framework can produce audio beyond the training distribution, reporting high-quality singing and music samples. They then increase both model size and training-set size to create DFlow-XL, a large universal vocoder. DFlow-XL performs competitively with BigVGAN, the leading universal vocoder identified in the abstract. Together, these results examine quality, speed, generalization, and the benefits of scaling the same framework.
icml-2024-dflow-a-generative-model-combi.tldr: DFlow combines normalizing flows with a denoising autoencoder to improve audio quality and synthesis speed, with a larger version competitive with BigVGAN.

paragraphs: A world model lets a reinforcement-learning agent predict how its environment evolves. Transformer-based world models can simulate environments effectively, but accurate simulation may require long token sequences and substantial computation. This paper introduces Δ-IRIS, an agent whose world model changes what is encoded and predicted to make that process more efficient.

The architecture has two complementary parts. A discrete autoencoder encodes stochastic changes between consecutive time steps. An autoregressive transformer predicts future changes while using continuous tokens to summarize the current world state. This separates the representation of the present from the representation of what changes next, making temporal context part of the tokenization and prediction design.

On the Crafter benchmark, Δ-IRIS achieves the best reported performance at several frame budgets. It also trains an order of magnitude faster than previous attention-based approaches. The findings therefore connect the architectural change to both learning performance and training efficiency in the evaluated environment. The contribution is a concrete example of improving a transformer world model by rethinking its representation of environmental change.
icml-2024-efficient-world-models-with-co.tldr: Δ-IRIS models changes between world states, achieving leading Crafter results while training an order of magnitude faster than previous attention-based approaches.

paragraphs: Generating plausible crystals is difficult because only a tiny fraction of atomic arrangements in periodic lattices are thermodynamically stable. FlowMM addresses two related tasks: finding a stable structure for a specified chemical composition, and proposing both new compositions and their structures. It supplies a pair of generative models for these different forms of materials discovery.

The method extends Riemannian Flow Matching to respect crystal symmetries, including translations, rotations, permutations of atoms, and periodic boundaries. These properties matter because different representations can describe equivalent crystal structures. The framework also permits different choices of starting distributions for the flow, which the authors report substantially simplifies learning crystal structures compared with diffusion approaches.

FlowMM achieves state-of-the-art results on both tasks in the reported benchmarks. The authors additionally use quantum chemistry calculations to assess generated structures. They find that FlowMM requires roughly three times fewer integration steps to find stable materials than previous open methods. That efficiency result specifically concerns integration steps, while the calculations provide evidence about the generated structures' stability.
icml-2024-flowmm-generating-materials-wi.tldr: FlowMM adapts flow matching to crystal symmetries, delivering leading generation results and finding stable materials with roughly threefold better integration-step efficiency.

paragraphs: Automated red teaming tests whether language models can be induced to produce harmful responses. Its usefulness depends partly on whether different testing methods and defenses can be compared fairly. HarmBench addresses the lack of a standardized evaluation framework, giving this research area a shared basis for assessing progress.

The authors identify desirable evaluation properties that earlier red-teaming assessments had not accounted for and design the framework around them. They then use HarmBench to compare 18 red-teaming methods against 33 target language models and defenses. This broad comparison makes the framework an instrument for studying both the effectiveness of attacks and the behavior of the systems they target.

The paper also introduces an efficient adversarial training method that substantially improves robustness across a wide range of tested attacks. This connects evaluation to model improvement: the same framework supports developing attacks and defenses together. The reported contribution therefore includes a shared evaluation approach, a large comparative study, and a training method whose robustness gains are demonstrated through that approach.
icml-2024-harmbench-a-standardized-evalu.tldr: HarmBench standardizes automated red-teaming evaluation and supports an efficient adversarial training method that improves robustness across many attacks.

paragraphs: Neural ordinary differential equations learn continuous dynamics, but their training and inference can be slow. This paper approaches that cost through control theory, asking how much depth the model needs to maintain its performance. It treats the terminal time of the dynamics as something to optimize alongside the network, connecting the duration of computation with the learning problem.

The authors propose two approaches. The first expresses training as a minimum-time optimal control problem and jointly searches for network weights and terminal time in one stage. This makes the desired computation duration part of the same optimization that determines the model's behavior.

The second approach separates the process into stages. It begins with pretraining and a Lyapunov method, then applies a safe mechanism for updating terminal time in the forward direction. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods can accelerate neural ODEs. Their shared contribution is to make depth selection an explicit part of training, with the aim of improving both training and inference speed while maintaining network performance.
icml-2024-how-deep-do-we-need-accelerati.tldr: Two control-theoretic approaches optimize neural ODE terminal time to accelerate training and inference while aiming to maintain performance.

paragraphs: Many text-to-3D systems depend on pretrained image generators and a procedure called score distillation sampling. That procedure can be slow, unstable, and prone to visual artifacts. IM-3D explores a different route: generate multiple views of an object and reconstruct a 3D asset from those views.

The key generation choice is to use a video generator rather than an image generator. The authors report that this substantially improves multiview generation. They combine the generated views with a reconstruction algorithm based on Gaussian splatting, which allows optimization of a robust image-based loss. The resulting pipeline directly converts the views into high-quality 3D outputs.

IM-3D reduces evaluations of the 2D generator network by a factor of 10 to 100. The paper reports a more efficient pipeline together with improved quality, fewer geometric inconsistencies, and a larger proportion of usable assets. These outcomes connect computational savings with practical output quality: reducing generator calls accompanies improvements in how successfully the views form a coherent 3D object.
icml-2024-im-3d-iterative-multiview-diff.tldr: IM-3D combines video-based multiview generation with Gaussian-splatting reconstruction to produce better 3D assets using 10–100 times fewer generator evaluations.

paragraphs: When edges enter a directed graph one at a time, a data structure must keep its vertices in a valid dependency order and detect whether a new edge creates a cycle. Strong worst-case algorithms can have expensive updates, while practical greedy approaches can also become costly in unfavorable cases. This paper uses predictions to improve the update process without surrendering worst-case protection.

The proposed data structure has three guarantees. With perfect predictions, it achieves the best possible running time. With poor predictions, its guarantees are no worse than those of the best-known worst-case methods. Between those extremes, its running time deteriorates smoothly as prediction error increases. These properties make prediction quality affect efficiency without leaving performance entirely dependent on accurate forecasts.

Experiments show substantial speedups on real datasets using predictions learned from a very small training dataset. The theoretical and empirical results address complementary concerns: the guarantees explain how the method handles prediction error, while the experiments show that useful predictions can be obtained with limited training data.
icml-2024-incremental-topological-orderi.tldr: A prediction-assisted graph data structure speeds up ordering and cycle detection while retaining worst-case guarantees and degrading smoothly with prediction error.

paragraphs: Binary classifiers are often assessed using the areas under ROC and precision-recall curves. These summaries capture different aspects of performance, so a strong value for one does not automatically establish a strong value for the other. This paper gives theoretical bounds that make the relationship between the two measures explicit.

The first theorem determines the largest and smallest precision-recall AUC compatible with a fixed ROC AUC. It shows how much precision-recall performance can vary even when ROC performance looks good, a concern especially relevant to imbalanced datasets. The second theorem works in the opposite direction, bounding ROC AUC when precision-recall AUC is fixed.

The authors also introduce a method for determining when an ordering of models under one measure implies an ordering under the other. This can clarify when comparing both metrics adds information and when a relationship can already be established. Their conclusions support prioritizing precision-recall AUC in certain settings, particularly some imbalanced problems, rather than treating either metric as universally preferable.
icml-2024-interplay-of-roc-and-precision.tldr: The paper derives bounds connecting ROC and precision-recall AUC, explaining when strong performance or model rankings under one metric transfer to the other.

paragraphs: Scientific point clouds can be large enough to make standard transformer processing expensive. HEPT addresses this problem with a transformer that incorporates local structure, achieves near-linear complexity, and uses regular computations suited to hardware. The intended applications include large point-cloud datasets in high-energy physics and astrophysics.

The paper first analyzes how different sparsification techniques trade approximation error against computational cost. Its findings favor locality-sensitive hashing, particularly combinations using OR and AND constructions, for kernel approximation when the data has useful local structure. This analysis supplies the basis for the architecture rather than introducing an efficiency mechanism without examining its approximation behavior.

HEPT combines E²LSH with those constructions and organizes the resulting operations into regular computations. On two high-energy physics tasks, it substantially outperforms the evaluated graph neural networks and transformers in both accuracy and speed. The result links three design goals: retaining local information, controlling approximation costs, and making the computations efficient to execute. The empirical performance claims concern the two reported physics tasks.
icml-2024-locality-sensitive-hashing-bas.tldr: HEPT uses locality-sensitive hashing to process large point clouds efficiently, improving accuracy and speed on two high-energy physics tasks.

paragraphs: When point data is rotated or reflected, useful learned features should often transform predictably with it. This property is called equivariance. The paper develops deep features equivariant to the rotations and reflections described by O(n), allowing the construction to apply to points in any dimension rather than only a particular spatial setting.

The proposed neurons use spherical decision surfaces and are built using hyperspheres and regular simplexes. The authors show how to assemble these Deep Equivariant Hyperspheres into a network operating directly on the input points. They also derive an invariant operator from the relationship between two points and a sphere, showing that it takes the form of a Gram matrix.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world data support the theoretical contributions. On the evaluated O(n)-equivariant classification and regression benchmarks, the approach outperforms competing methods and offers a favorable balance of speed and performance. The contribution combines a geometric neuron design with a way to construct both predictably transforming features and invariant information for downstream predictions.
icml-2024-o-n-learning-deep-o-n-equivari.tldr: Deep Equivariant Hyperspheres use spherical neurons to learn rotation- and reflection-equivariant features in arbitrary dimensions, with strong reported benchmark results.

paragraphs: Structured pruning reduces inference cost by removing whole components such as neurons or attention heads, allowing savings on standard deep-learning hardware. OSSCAR focuses on pruning after training without requiring subsequent retraining. The challenge is selecting which structures to remove while keeping the remaining network's behavior useful.

The authors formulate selection as a combinatorial optimization problem with an objective that reconstructs each layer's output. A reformulation makes optimization scalable, and a local search algorithm uses low-rank updates to evaluate changes efficiently. This connects the discrete choice of retained structures to a reconstruction objective while managing both time and memory costs.

OSSCAR improves on the evaluated one-shot methods across vision and language models, including models with tens of billions of parameters. For the reported OPT-2.7B example, it can deliver 125 times lower WikiText perplexity and twice the inference speed compared with ZipLM. The pruning framework is also reported to run six to eight times faster. These comparisons distinguish the quality and speed of the pruned model from the cost of carrying out pruning.
icml-2024-osscar-one-shot-structured-pru.tldr: OSSCAR uses efficient combinatorial optimization to prune large vision and language models without retraining, improving reported model quality and computational efficiency.

paragraphs: Nonlinear optimal control seeks controllers that act optimally in systems with nonlinear dynamics, and the problem becomes especially challenging in high dimensions. This paper develops model-based policy-iteration algorithms with convergence guarantees. Their central step repeatedly uses neural approximations to solve linear partial differential equations.

Two variants address that step differently. The first turns the optimization into a linear least-squares problem, drawing on extreme learning machines, and achieves efficient, accurate solutions for low-dimensional problems. The second uses physics-informed neural networks to solve the equations and has the potential to handle high-dimensional problems. The abstract presents that higher-dimensional capability as a prospect rather than a universal demonstrated result.

The authors report substantial improvements over traditional approaches such as Galerkin methods. They also analyze convergence of the neural approximations toward the true optimal solutions in a general setting. Finally, formal verification techniques establish verifiable stability of the resulting controllers. The work therefore addresses both obtaining good control solutions and providing mathematical evidence about convergence and controller stability.
icml-2024-physics-informed-neural-networ.tldr: Neural PDE solvers support two policy-iteration algorithms with convergence analysis, improved reported control results, and formally verified controller stability.

paragraphs: Responsible AI licenses include clauses governing how released software or models may be used. They are intended to help developers address negligent or malicious applications while distributing AI assets. This position paper examines their adoption and adaptation, then argues that standardization is necessary to preserve their usefulness as adoption grows.

The authors combine qualitative interviews, clustering of license clauses, and quantitative analysis of adoption. These methods examine both why organizations choose such licenses and how they modify restrictions for particular situations. The abstract reports adoption across roughly 40,000 repositories by the end of 2023, making variation in license language a practical issue for many users.

The authors' position is that inconsistent clauses can confuse users or weaken the licenses' impact. They also recognize that some settings, such as medical applications, warrant tailored behavioral restrictions. Their proposed direction is standardized customization: shared conventions that still accommodate appropriate variation and can be supported by tools. This is an evidence-informed recommendation about license design, balancing consistency with the needs of distinct application contexts.
icml-2024-position-standardization-of-be.tldr: The authors argue for standardized but customizable responsible AI licenses to reduce confusion while accommodating domain-specific behavioral restrictions.

paragraphs: Green AI emphasizes the sustainability and inclusivity of AI research, making efficiency part of how research value is assessed. This position paper argues that tensor networks deserve serious consideration within that agenda. Its case rests on their mathematical foundations and their potential for logarithmic compression.

The authors review discussions of Green AI and assemble an overview of efficiency metrics proposed in that literature. They then use those metrics to evaluate tensor-network examples in kernel machines and deep learning. This links the broader argument to concrete ways of assessing efficiency, rather than presenting compression potential alone as sufficient evidence of practical value.

The paper's conclusion is a research recommendation: investigate tensor networks as a possible tool for making AI more sustainable and accessible, and give Green AI principles greater priority. The stated contribution is the connection between these research areas, supported by a review and evaluated examples. It presents tensor networks as a valuable option to examine within particular projects, with efficiency metrics providing a basis for that examination.
icml-2024-position-tensor-networks-are-a.tldr: This position paper argues that tensor networks' mathematical structure and compression potential make them valuable candidates for sustainable, inclusive AI research.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks classify nodes using connected data, yet their training objectives commonly sum losses that treat node labels independently. The paper argues that this mismatch restricts generalization and resistance to adversarial attacks. It proposes changing the supervision objective so that a node's label is learned together with information from its local cluster.

The resulting framework, joint-cluster supervised learning, models the joint distribution of node and cluster labels conditioned on their representations. It trains the network using the associated joint loss. This gives the target node explicit reference signals from its surrounding cluster, strengthening the information used to distinguish its class.

Experiments show improved node-classification accuracy and substantial protection against the evaluated adversarial attacks. The proposed explanation is that cluster reference signals may remain unaffected when malicious interference targets other information used for classification. That qualification matters: the framework benefits from potentially cleaner contextual signals. Its contribution is therefore a way to incorporate graph relationships directly into supervision, with reported gains in both prediction accuracy and robustness.
icml-2024-rethinking-independent-cross-e.tldr: Joint-cluster supervision trains graph networks on node and cluster labels together, improving reported classification accuracy and adversarial robustness.

paragraphs: Online continual learning trains a model from a stream in which classification tasks appear sequentially and incoming data can be seen only once. This makes preserving useful knowledge especially challenging. Replay-based strategies have become prominent, while knowledge distillation has received less attention in this online setting despite its use in offline continual learning.

The paper analyzes the obstacles to applying distillation under these constraints and supplies empirical support for that analysis. It then introduces a straightforward way to add momentum knowledge distillation to several leading online continual-learning methods. The approach is presented as a component that improves existing methods, allowing the authors to examine its contribution across multiple learning strategies.

On ImageNet100, the reported improvement over existing state-of-the-art accuracy exceeds ten percentage points. The authors also investigate how momentum distillation behaves during training and how it affects the learning process. Based on these findings, they argue that it should be treated as a central component of online continual learning alongside replay. That recommendation follows from the demonstrated gains and analysis of its training behavior.
icml-2024-rethinking-momentum-knowledge-.tldr: Adding momentum knowledge distillation improves several online continual-learning methods, including a reported gain exceeding ten accuracy percentage points on ImageNet100.

paragraphs: Robust Markov games model strategic decisions when aspects of the game are uncertain. This paper studies games with s-rectangular uncertainty and connects their robust Nash equilibria to ordinary Nash equilibria in suitably regularized games. The equivalence offers another mathematical route to computing strategies that account for uncertainty.

The connection yields a planning algorithm and provable robustness guarantees for policies obtained through regularized methods. However, converting the formulation does not make every instance easy to solve. The authors prove that finding a robust equilibrium is PPAD-hard even for two-player, zero-sum matrix games where only rewards are uncertain, establishing a substantial computational obstacle within a restricted setting.

They then identify an uncertainty structure called efficient player-decomposability. For two-player, zero-sum robust Markov games in this class, robust equilibria can be computed in polynomial time. The class includes commonly used L1 and L-infinity ball uncertainty sets. Together, the results explain both how regularization relates to robustness and which additional structure makes the corresponding equilibrium computation provably efficient.
icml-2024-roping-in-uncertainty-robustne.tldr: The paper links robust equilibria to regularized games, proves general computational hardness, and identifies an uncertainty class permitting efficient solutions.

paragraphs: Recovering a signal from a noisy matrix becomes more complicated when noise has different structure across blocks. This paper studies that situation through the inhomogeneous Wigner spike model. Its goal is to find an optimal spectral method and characterize the point at which spectral information begins to reveal the hidden signal.

The authors rigorously analyze a transformed matrix. They track two events: an eigenvalue separating from the main body of the limiting spectrum, and its associated eigenvector acquiring positive overlap with the signal. The first is a visible change in the spectrum; the second establishes that the corresponding direction contains useful information about the signal.

They show that both transitions occur exactly at the optimal threshold for the studied problem. This extends the familiar BBP transition criterion from homogeneous noise to the block-structured setting. The proposed method is optimal within the class of iterative methods for this inhomogeneous Wigner problem. The result therefore connects a precisely characterized spectral transition with an optimality guarantee for that specific model and method class.
icml-2024-spectral-phase-transition-and-.tldr: A transformed-matrix spectral method reaches the optimal iterative-method recovery threshold in a Wigner model with block-structured noise.

paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented generation supplies a language model with documents relevant to a question. Large retrieved contexts can increase computational cost and introduce irrelevant material that degrades answers. Superposition prompting addresses both issues through a prompting method that works with pretrained transformer language models without requiring fine-tuning.

The method organizes documents into parallel prompt paths. The model processes those paths and discards ones judged irrelevant, limiting continued processing of unhelpful context. This organization connects efficiency with relevance: reducing unnecessary document processing also addresses the distraction caused by material that does not help answer the question.

Across multiple language models and question-answering benchmarks, the authors demonstrate improved time efficiency. Accuracy improves substantially when retrieved context is large relative to the context used in training. In one reported example, MPT-7B on NaturalQuestions-Open uses 93 times less compute time while improving accuracy by 43% relative to naive retrieval-augmented generation. That example illustrates the potential size of the gains in a particular setting, alongside the broader evidence for efficiency improvements.
icml-2024-superposition-prompting-improv.tldr: Superposition prompting processes retrieved documents in parallel paths and drops irrelevant ones, improving RAG efficiency and accuracy without fine-tuning.

paragraphs: State-space models carry a recurrent state, suggesting that they might track sequential changes more effectively than transformers. This paper asks whether that architectural appearance translates into greater expressive power. Its theoretical analysis finds closely related limitations in the state-space models studied and in transformers.

The authors place the models' expressive power within the complexity class TC0. They connect that limit to an inability to express certain state-tracking computations, including permutation composition. The analysis also establishes consequences for accurately tracking chess moves in certain notation, evaluating code, and following entities through long narratives. These are claims about the formal computational capabilities analyzed, not simply about whether a model stores an internal vector called a state.

Experiments with Mamba-style models supplement the theory and show difficulty with state tracking. Together, the results challenge the assumption that a recurrent formulation alone supplies the sequential reasoning capabilities associated with recurrent networks. The authors conclude that the shared expressiveness limitations may fundamentally constrain performance on real-world tasks that require this kind of state tracking.
icml-2024-the-illusion-of-state-in-state.tldr: The paper finds that the analyzed state-space models share transformers' formal state-tracking limitations, supported by experiments with Mamba-style models.
